title: Her parents: teacher mother, father a railroad man turned lawyer
summary: Humes describes her mother the school teacher and her father, a railroad man who studied law and became one of Louisville's first black attorneys, then a real estate man. He died in 1975 near age 97; she recalls few other relatives.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, if you want me to start there, alright. Well, I had the best parents in the world, I'll say that, because they were. Well, my mother used to be a school teacher and my father, he was, well in the earlier days he was a railroad man, and then he went to law school and he studied to be an attorney. And then in the later years he was a real estate man.
Helen, about your father being an attorney, wasn't that a little unusual in those days?
Yes it was a little unusual especially in the South. But he was one of the first black attorneys in Louieville.

And that would have been 1910, or something like that, wouldn't it?
When we talked about it you thought probably your father was born in about 1978.
I know he died in 1975 and if he had lived until July he would have been 97. But he died in January, January 3rd. I suppose he was 96 1/2.
Was members of his family, were they all long lived people? Did they have long lives?
Well, I didn't know too much about them. I knew I had a cousin. Her name was Mildred. And then I had an Uncle Ed. But they all died, you know, they died when I was young.
Yes. And I didn't know too much about them.
Well your father certainly had a long life.
